_comment: Reference run — same DDIM 16/eta0/n1 as the per-eval AR-corpus hook used during training. Establishes the ablation's baseline against the runs/exp_014_diffusion/metrics.jsonl numbers (matched_rate hit max 0.519 at E5).
name: ddim_16_e0_n1

_comment: n_samples=4 mean-of-softmax marginalization. THE headline question — does aggregating 4 independent x_T draws fix the dense/sparse bistability that flipped matched_rate 0.18 ↔ 0.52 between adjacent training evals? If yes, sampler variance was the issue. If matched_rate barely moves, denoiser quality is the bottleneck.
name: ddim_16_e0_n4

_comment: Cheapest sampler — 4 DDIM steps. If matched_rate is comparable to 16-step (within ~2 pp), inference can be 4× faster for free. If it craters, the schedule's high-t end matters and we need more steps.
name: ddim_4_e0_n1

_comment: Upper bound — full-schedule 64-step DDPM with eta=1 (paper-spec). If even this can't beat ddim_16 by >3 pp, the bottleneck is not in the sampler — it's in the denoiser / decode_to_logits soft-margin issue. Most expensive variant; place it early so its result informs whether to bother running the rest.
name: ddpm_64_e1_n1

_comment: Stochastic single-sample DDIM (eta=1). Tests whether deterministic eta=0 is better than per-step Brownian noise injection — the paper says eta=0 is sharper for image gen; here we want to confirm.
name: ddim_16_e1_n1

_comment: Fill-in — 32 steps eta=0. If 32 doesn't substantially beat 16, more deterministic steps don't help.
name: ddim_32_e0_n1
